messages:
raj: Heads up — staging canary for service-a (v2.7.1) blocked by deploybot SBOM flag. Deploybot says missing provenance for libfoo@1.3. Change window in ~2h. Do we pin, vendor, or stall?

deploybot: Automated block: SBOM provenance mismatch on image service-a:sha256:9f8e...
Reason: missing source/checksum for dependency 'libfoo@1.3'. Approvals required from security. See scan: https://ci/scan/1735

olivia: Is this likely a false positive? I built locally and SBOM lists libfoo@1.3 but no signature field.

max_sre: If we stall, canary schedule slides. Hotpatch vs stall tradeoffs. How long would a rebuild take?

jen_security: Need the SBOM snippet + artifact metadata (image digest, build id). Policy: no provenance = either pin to vetted version, vendor dependency with documented source+hash, or stall for resign.

raj: Pasting the minimal SBOM lines below (from the artifact):

olivia: ```json
{"name":"libfoo","version":"1.3","purl":"pkg:npm/libfoo@1.3"}
```

jen_security: That SBOM lacks checksum/signature and source. Two options: 1) short stall and ask builder to re-run with signing (timebox 4h), 2) temp mitigation (pin to vetted libfoo@1.2 OR vendor lib into image) and proceed with canary in staging only, with post-deploy remediation. Which is acceptable? :thinking:

raj: 4h stall would kill today’s change window. We prefer an interim mitigation if low blast radius.

max_sre: Pin to 1.2 might ripple deps. Vendoring might be faster but requires rebuild + CI. Estimate: vendoring ~1.5h, pinning potentially longer.

olivia: I can vendor libfoo into the image (copy source + add SBOM entry with build hash) and trigger a rebuild. Should be ~90 mins. Is vendoring compliant as interim?

jen_security: Vendoring is acceptable as interim if you add an SBOM entry that includes source URL, build commit and file checksum, and mark it as 'temp-vendored' in metadata. Security will do expedited checks. Also require explicit note in release notes about temporary change and rollback plan.

raj: Proposal: Olivia vendors + rebuild; deploybot keeps artifact in quarantine until security confirms SBOM/provenance; proceed with canary in staging only if security signs off; keep production on hold until full provenance is restored. Ack?

olivia: Ack — starting vendoring and build now. Will push new image and notify.

deploybot: Action logged: set artifact state -> quarantine. Notifying security. Will re-scan on new artifact upload.

jen_security: I'll watch the CI run and re-scan. If SBOM includes checksum+vendor tag, I'll grant staging-only approval. :white_check_mark:

raj: Please include rollback steps & oncall contacts in release notes. I'll draft: "temporary vendored libfoo due to missing SBOM provenance; will revert to signed upstream once available; contact oncall@redwood if regressions."

max_sre: Add explicit rollback command: `kubectl set image deploy/service-a service-a=service-a@sha256:abcdef` and oncall pager. Keep 30m observation window for canary.

olivia: Build pushed: https://ci/build/34567 — triggered SBOM scan.

deploybot: New artifact uploaded; SBOM re-scan queued.

jen_security: CI SBOM now shows vendor tag, checksum, and build hash. Security approves staging canary only.

deploybot: Quarantine lifted for staging canary; production remains on hold until full upstream provenance restored.

raj: Monitoring canary metrics now. If any regression, rollback to image sha256:abcdef within 30m.

olivia: If rollback needed ping @olivia immediately.

jen_security: Post-action: file a short remediation ticket to get libfoo properly signed or upgrade to signed upstream. Security will verify full fix before production.

raj: Thanks everyone. Closing thread once canary passes.
